online-softmax.name: online softmax
online-softmax.definition: A recurrence that updates a stable softmax maximum and shifted denominator incrementally.
online-softmax.explanation: Online softmax keeps a running maximum and a denominator made from exponentials shifted by that maximum. When a larger score appears, it rescales the old denominator to the new reference before adding the new shifted mass. Those two values are normalization state rather than probabilities or learned weights. Attention can carry a value-weighted numerator on the same scale and divide only after all permitted key positions have contributed.

tiled-attention.name: tiled attention
tiled-attention.definition: Attention evaluated over bounded blocks of query or key positions.
tiled-attention.explanation: This chapter tiles key positions for one query row at a time, computes a small score vector, and merges it with compact running normalization state. Every causally permitted query-key pair is still evaluated, so dense arithmetic remains quadratic in sequence positions. The scalar oracle already avoids a full quadratic intermediate by storing one score row; tiling reduces that temporary row to a bounded block. Hardware speed depends on block shapes, fusion, and the memory hierarchy.

grouped-query-attention.name: grouped-query attention
grouped-query-attention.definition: Several query heads sharing each key and value head.
grouped-query-attention.explanation: Grouped-query attention uses Hq query heads but fewer Hkv key/value heads. Equal contiguous groups of Hq/Hkv query heads read one shared K/V head. It interpolates between ordinary multi-head attention, where counts match, and multi-query attention, where one K/V head serves every query head. In a decoder this can reduce K/V projection parameters and cache storage, though dense pairwise attention work still grows quadratically with sequence positions.

checks: Tiled attention matches the scalar oracle within 2e-6 + 2e-6 times absolute reference across key-tile widths
First causal output equals its only visible value
Increasing maxima preserve a hand-computed weighted numerator
Invalid or overflowing shapes and nonfinite scores are rejected
GQA requires a divisible head mapping
A maximum-sized tile does not overflow index arithmetic
limitations: Scalar CPU code demonstrates the recurrence, not FlashAttention hardware performance
Scalar oracle stores one score row rather than an entire quadratic tensor
Random tensors do not measure trained-model quality
No backward pass or block-sparse approximation is implemented
Benchmark measures allocating end-to-end CPU functions, not allocation-free kernels
